data.label: Receive SIEM Alert
data.description: Trigger the workflow when the SIEM system raises a security alert.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on an external SIEM signal. No ML, NLP, or LLM behavior is needed; it is pure workflow activation logic.

data.label: Assess Alert Severity
data.description: Review the alert severity to determine the urgency and response path.
data.rationale: Severity is typically a structured field from the SIEM or alert payload and can be handled with deterministic rules or mapping tables. L0 is sufficient unless severity must be inferred from noisy free text, which is not indicated here.

data.label: Check IP Reputation
data.description: Evaluate the source IP against reputation and threat intelligence sources.
data.rationale: This step requires querying external reputation/threat-intelligence sources and combining those results with the workflow context. The lookup itself could be deterministic, but the multi-source API/tool interaction makes this tool-augmented automation (L4).

data.label: Identify Affected Assets
data.description: Determine which endpoints, servers, or other assets are impacted by the alert.
data.rationale: Identifying impacted assets usually requires querying CMDB, EDR, SIEM, or asset inventory systems to correlate indicators with infrastructure. Because it depends on multiple external data sources and possibly iterative lookups, L4 is appropriate.

data.label: Determine Alert Disposition
data.description: Decide whether the alert is critical or a false positive based on triage findings.
data.rationale: This is a rules-based decision step that can be implemented with deterministic branching over triage outputs such as severity, IP reputation, and asset impact. No learning or language reasoning is required from the description.

data.label: Isolate Endpoint
data.description: Immediately isolate the affected endpoint to contain a critical incident.
data.rationale: Endpoint isolation is an external action executed through an EDR, MDM, or endpoint containment API. The action is deterministic, but it requires tool invocation against an external system, so L4 fits.

data.label: Notify Security Team
data.description: Send an urgent incident notification to the security team via PagerDuty.
data.rationale: Sending the notification requires calling PagerDuty or a similar incident-management API. The content may be templated, but the external tool/API integration makes this L4.

data.label: Run Forensic Scan
data.description: Collect logs, memory dumps, and network traffic captures from affected systems.
data.rationale: This step orchestrates collection across security and system tooling to gather logs, memory, and network evidence. It is a multi-tool operational workflow, not pure logic, so L4 is appropriate.

data.label: Correlate Findings
data.description: Analyze and correlate evidence across multiple data sources to identify the attack vector.
data.rationale: Correlating evidence across multiple data sources requires dynamic reasoning over heterogeneous inputs. A single LLM could summarize findings, but the workflow implies iterative evidence gathering and cross-source analysis with tools, making L4 the best fit. Confidence is lower because the exact method of correlation is not specified and could range from deterministic rules to LLM-assisted analysis.

data.label: Generate Incident Report
data.description: Compile the incident timeline, impact assessment, and remediation recommendations.
data.rationale: This is primarily a language-generation and summarization task: compile a report from collected facts into a readable incident narrative. A single LLM call can generate the report without requiring external tools, so L3 is sufficient.

data.label: Update SIEM Rules
data.description: Adjust SIEM detection rules to reduce recurrence of the false positive pattern.
data.rationale: Updating SIEM rules usually means editing configuration through a SIEM API or rules engine and possibly validating the updated rule set. That is deterministic but tool-driven operational automation, so L4 applies.

data.label: Document False Positive
data.description: Record the false positive pattern and tuning notes for future reference.
data.rationale: This step is a documentation/summarization task that transforms triage context into a written record. A single LLM call can draft the note without external tools, so L3 is appropriate.

message: This workflow is primarily deterministic security orchestration with several tool-augmented operational steps. L0 covers the trigger, severity assessment, and disposition logic; L3 is used for report/document generation; L4 is used for API-driven actions such as IP reputation checks, endpoint isolation, PagerDuty notifications, forensic collection, and SIEM rule updates. No multi-agent collaboration is necessary, so L5 is not used.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a security alert is triggered by the SIEM system, triage the alert by checking severity, source IP reputation, and affected assets. For critical alerts, immediately isolate the affected endpoint and notify the security team via PagerDuty. Run an automated forensic scan to collect logs, memory dumps, and network traffic captures. Correlate findings across multiple data sources to identify the attack vector. Generate an incident report with timeline, impact assessment, and recommended remediation steps. For false positives, update the SIEM rules and document the false positive pattern for future tuning.
